title: Summarized Route Insight Card: MVP consolidation for cost + trace surface
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Proposal to collapse multiple route-level UI surfaces (per-route microcards + separate cost breakdown page + aggressive tracing embeds) into one summarized Route Insight Card for the Console MVP. Aim is to preserve essential operator workflows (quick cost attribution, recent high-latency spikes, and trace linkouts) while cutting surface area to meet scope and engineering constraints.
background: During alpha reviews we identified three competing cards for route observability: per-route microcards (high-cardinality), a dedicated cost breakdown page, and embedded detailed traces. Each adds engineering and telemetry overhead. Team capacity for Q1 is constrained and backend telemetry payloads are expensive. PM + Design propose an aggregation approach to reduce implementation scope while keeping key signals for early users.
goals: Deliver a single Route Insight Card that summarizes cost-per-1000 tokens, 95th latency, and top 3 error reasons
Provide a clear call-to-action for drilldown to existing Trace Explorer (link only) rather than embedding full traces
Reduce frontend card count by >=70% on routes overview page to cut render and telemetry cost
Keep rollout safe with gradual visibility flags and fallback defaults to legacy behavior
scope_included: One Route Insight Card component on Routes list and Route detail
Cost summary metric (rolling 7d cost per 1k tokens) with sparkline
Latency metric (p95) with sparkline and anomaly flag when > SLO
CTA: 'Open trace' links to Trace Explorer with pre-filled filter params (no embedded traces)
Feature flag gating + feature rollout config in Console feature-flag service
scope_cut: Per-route microcards for every route variant (defer to future phase)
Inline trace embedding and trace timeline visualization
Full cost breakdown per token-type in card (moved to separate Cost UI backlog)
Automatic sampling controls and advanced trace sampling UI
High-cardinality real-time streaming of token-level metrics
acceptance_criteria: Route overview page shows a single Route Insight Card for each route in the listing when feature flag is enabled
Card displays cost per 1k tokens and p95 latency with sparkline for the last 7 days
Clicking the 'Open trace' CTA opens Trace Explorer in a new tab with route and time filter populated
Anomaly badge appears when p95 crosses configured SLO threshold; QA verifies threshold logic against test telemetry fixtures
Backend exposes a consolidated route_metrics API: metrics: cost_7d_per_1k, p95_7d, error_buckets_top3 — API contract must be documented and stubbed for frontend integration tests
Feature flag supports user-level targeting; rollout to 10% orgs in first week and ability to rollback within 1 hour
Telemetry emitted includes event:route_card_render with dimensions route_id, variant, flag_state; volume drop measured in staging vs alpha must approximate >60% reduction in card render events
Accessibility: card meets basic keyboard navigation and screen reader label checks (AX-101 checklist)
decision_log: 2025-01-12: Chose aggregated card over microcards to reduce initial engineering and telemetry cost (PM + Eng + Design consensus)
2025-01-18: Decided to link out to Trace Explorer instead of embedding traces to avoid increasing bundle size and trace-query costs (Eng lead: Priya Shah)
2025-01-22: Agreed to postpone per-token cost breakdown to Cost UI initiative; kept single summary metric for MVP (Finance requested deferred breakdown)
2025-01-29: Rollout strategy approved: feature-flag + 10% pilot orgs, metrics-driven expansion
tradeoffs: Consolidating into a single card reduces immediate scope and cost but sacrifices fast inline exploration for power users. Linking out to Trace Explorer preserves full-fidelity investigation at the expense of a context switch. We accept this temporary UX cost to hit the Q1 ship date and reduce telemetry overhead.
risks: Power users may perceive reduced discoverability for per-route insights and request restoration
Trace Explorer filters must be reliable; link mismatch will lead to frustrated users (QA gating)
Backend aggregation API could become a bottleneck if not paginated or cached
Feature flag rollback must be tested end-to-end to avoid partial states during rollout
next_steps: Week 1 (Design + PM): Finalize visual spec and microcopy for the single card
Week 1 (Eng): Backend contract sketch and telemetry budget estimate; implement stubbed route_metrics endpoint
Week 2 (Eng): Frontend component scaffold and feature-flag wiring; integrate stub API
Week 3 (QA): E2E tests for render, CTA link correctness, anomaly badge behavior
Week 4 (Pilot): Enable feature for 10% pilot orgs, monitor telemetry and cost delta; review after 7 days
notes: This ticket intentionally aims to be a pragmatic slice: minimal visual complexity, explicit CTA for deeper investigation, and strict telemetry economy. If pilot metrics show unacceptable UX regression, we will re-prioritize per-route microcards as a follow-up with additional engineering budget.
